panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is the direct fluorescent antibody test (FAT) on a brain smear from a human rabies isolate, showing the classic apple-green fluorescence of rabies virus nucleoprotein; this is the textbook diagnostic manifestation of rabies and the finding key rabies_rabies_antigen_immunostaining applies. Human-patient-derived diagnostic microscopy with direct rabies attribution. B: High-magnification confocal laser scanning microscopy of cerebral tissue from the human rabies isolate showing rabies virus phosphoprotein (RABV-P, green) with blue nuclear counterstain; a direct rabies antigen immunostaining finding in patient-derived tissue. No Negri-body H&E evidence is claimed here. C: Lower-magnification (100 µm scale) confocal overview of cerebral tissue from the same human rabies isolate showing disseminated RABV-P antigen (green) among cell nuclei (blue); again a direct rabies immunostaining manifestation in patient-derived brain tissue.

in_text_mentions: There was a terminal bronchopneumonia. The heart had mild interstitial T-cell inflammation, and neuritis of vagus nerve branches, including a possible Negri body on Haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stain (Figure 2), but immunohistochemistry did not confirm this as rabies antigen. The tongue (Figure 3a) and parotid gland also had peri- and endoneural inflammation and ganglionitis.

The brain and meninges were grossly normal; there was no cerebral swelling. Histologically, there was mild encephalitis (T-cell infiltration, perivascular cuffing and microgliosis), most prominent in temporal lobes. Neuronal rabies infection with abundant Negri bodies (round/oval eosinophilic inclusions in the perikaryon) was present in all parts of cerebrum and sub-tentorial brain tissue, most prominently in the temporal lobe and hippocampus (Figure 3b). No hypoxic-ischaemic neurone damage was identified; only rare neurones were undergoing necrosis with sattelitosis.

RABV antigen and nucleic acid were widely distributed in central nervous system (CNS) and non-CNS tissues post mortem (Figure 3). All brain regions were strongly positive for RABV antigen using FAT; live virus was isolated from brain and cerebrospinal fluid in tissue culture at first passage. No neutralizing antibodies were detected in CSF by FAVN. Although viral RNA was detected in tongue, parotid salivary gland and a mouth swab taken post mortem, live virus was not recovered from these samples. Viral RNA was not detected in heart tissue.
